test/control_plane/policy-seed.test.ts::section 4 -- gate stage tolerances > exactly the stage tolerances of section 4 are seeded
entries.reason: The source compares a dict keyed by the (gate_type, stage) tuple against the transcribed GATE_STAGE_TOLERANCE dict. JavaScript has no tuple keys, so both sides are built as (gate_type, stage, tolerance_ms) triples and compared as sorted arrays with toEqual. This is at least as strong: a duplicated (gate_type, stage) pair would silently collapse in the Python dict comprehension and fails the array comparison here. Values, including the NULL/null tolerances, are compared unchanged.

entries.reason: The source uses sets of (gate_type, stage) tuples with `timed <= owned` and a scan over `timed | owned`. JavaScript Sets compare by reference for arrays, so membership is taken over a Set of JSON-serialized pairs and the subset check is a per-pair assertion (which also names the offending pair on failure); the union scan becomes a scan over the concatenation, which is equivalent for the `any(stage == 'forwarded')` predicate. Both assertions of the source are kept.

inherited_limitations.topic: The expectation tables are transcribed from docs/time-base-policy.md by hand, not derived from 0002_policy_seed.sql.
inherited_limitations.status: inherited, and the point of the file
inherited_limitations.detail: DETECTION_LATENCY, GATE_STAGE_TOLERANCE, the ownership table and RECONCILE_PERIOD_MS are deliberate duplication: the test is the comparison between two independently written copies of the same decision. A helper that generated the expectations from the migration would assert only that SQLite can read back what it stored. Reproduced exactly as in the source.

inherited_limitations.topic: 'no stage carries a tolerance without a ball holder to name' is vacuous if the tolerance set is empty.
inherited_limitations.detail: The source asserts the set relation `timed <= owned`, which is trivially true for an empty `timed`; the port expands it to a per-pair assertion, which is vacuous in the same case and for the same reason. Neither side would catch a regression that dropped every non-NULL tolerance. Adding a non-empty guard would make the port stronger than its source, so it is disclosed instead.

inherited_limitations.topic: The supersession cases assert the original revision's row count is unchanged, not that the copy inserted the expected number of rows.
inherited_limitations.detail: Neither the source nor the port asserts that the copying INSERT ... SELECT actually wrote `original` rows under the later revision, so an INSERT that wrote nothing would still pass. Faithful to interlock at 65f36c5.

inherited_limitations.topic: The standing-owner comparison keys by gate_type from a SELECT DISTINCT.
inherited_limitations.detail: A gate type carrying two different standing owners collapses to whichever row came last, so the equality can pass on data the assertion means to reject. Present identically in the source.
